City Data · Illinois

Chicago, Illinois

A city profile of outcomes for people with disabilities, from the ADA-PARC City Data tool.

Based on ACS 2024 5-Year Estimates, of the city’s 2,686,889 residents, 324,587 (12.1%) are people with disabilities.
% With Disability0.0%-9.6%9.6%-13.2%13.2%-17.6%17.6%-100.0%No data

Summary: This map shows the percent of residents with disabilities in each census tract in Chicago. Tract rates ranged from 0.8% to 54.1%. Data was available for 798 of 801 census tracts.

This report is sourced from: Based on 2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates

Disability Demographics

For each Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age group below, the headline figure is that group’s share of the city’s total population, with the number of people that represents shown underneath it. Hispanic/Latino is an ethnicity that can include people of any race, so it overlaps with the race categories above it, and figures across groups are not meant to sum to the city total.

Age

The Census asks about hearing and vision difficulty at every age, but the other four disability types (cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, and independent living) are only asked starting at age 5, and independent living only from age 15. The “Under 5” figure below reflects hearing and vision difficulty alone, so it is not directly comparable to the other age groups, which draw on more disability types.

  • Under 50.04% of the city’s total population1,018 residents

  • Ages 18 to 646.4% of the city’s total population173,224 residents
  • Ages 65 and older4.9% of the city’s total population130,441 residents

Disability Types

Each percentage below is the share of the city’s total population, not just the population with disabilities, that reports that specific type of disability. A person can have more than one type, and many do, so these categories overlap. The six figures below will add up to more than the city’s overall disability rate, often to about twice it, and are not meant to sum to the total.

  • Hearing2.4% of the city’s total population64,409 residents

Community Living

Housing Access

Among households in each HUD-assisted housing program, the share with a head of household or spouse/co-head who has a disability. This is a rate within an already-assisted population, not a citywide figure, so it should not be compared directly to the disability rate shown elsewhere on this page. A missing figure usually means the city has no households reported in that program, not a suppressed or unpublished value.

  • Housing Choice Vouchers — 36.0%
  • Public Housing — 31.0%

Living arrangement measures, covering whether people with disabilities live at home, in non-institutional group quarters, or in a nursing home or correctional facility, are not available for individual cities. The Census publishes the underlying tables (S2601A, S2602, B26108) only for the nation, states and larger regions, so these measures appear on the National Data tab rather than here. This is a limit in how the Census releases group quarters data, not a gap in this pipeline. A partial estimate for the largest cities, built from Census microdata, is under development for a future update.

The ADA-PARC is funded by the National Institute for Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research (NIDILRR) under grants 90DP0026 and 90DPAD0001.
